title: 2.2 Consistency Error Taxonomy
use_cases: Use when evaluating the narrative integrity of LLM-generated stories
Implement when benchmarking long-form creative writing models
Configure when setting up automated quality gates for character consistency
Use when categorizing specific failures in world-building or setting logic
Implement when developing error-detection pipelines for synthetic narrative data
content:
To enable systematic evaluation, we develop a hierarchical taxonomy grounded in narrative theory and prior research on story understanding (Ismayilzada et al., 2024; Xie et al., 2023). The taxonomy comprises five top-level categories and 19 fine-grained error types (Table 2), encompassing contradictions that emerge across temporal logic, character memory, world-building rules, factual details, and narrative style. Representative error cases with detailed annotations are presented in Figure 2.

Table 2: Consistency-error taxonomy used by ConStory-Bench, comprising five categories and 19 subtypes.

| Error Type | Sub Error Type |
| --- | --- |
| Timeline & Plot | Absolute Time Contradictions |
| Logic | Duration Contradictions |
| Simultaneity Contradictions |
| Causeless Effects |
| Causal Logic Violations |
| Abandoned Plot Elements |
| Characterization | Memory Contradictions |
| Knowledge Contradictions |
| Skill Fluctuations |
| Forgotten Abilities |
| World-building & | Core Rules Violations |
| Setting | Social Norms Violations |
| Geographical Contradictions |
| Factual & Detail | Appearance Mismatches |
| Consistency | Nomenclature Confusions |
| Quantitative Mismatches |
| Narrative & Style | Perspective Confusions |
| Tone Inconsistencies |
| Style Shifts |
